Current Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative (K/DOQI) treatment guidelines for vitamin D deficiency in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) on ergocalciferol (vitamin D3 supplementation) have been found to be inadequate. The guidelines recommend increasing the dose of vitamin D or using higher dosages, but they do not provide sufficient evidence for these measures.

The current K/DOQI treatment guidelines are based on studies that used lower doses of ergocalciferol and did not investigate the effects of higher or more frequent dosing on clinical outcomes. These limitations make it difficult to determine whether increasing vitamin D dosage would improve treatment effectiveness in CKD patients with vitamin D deficiency.

Future research is needed to investigate the effects of ergocalciferol dosing strategies, such as higher or more frequent doses, and to evaluate their impact on clinical endpoints, including vitamin D levels, secondary hyperparathyroidism, and mortality. As a result, current K/DOQI treatment guidelines are inadequate for correcting vitamin D deficiency in CKD patients treated with ergocalciferol.

In summary, while ergocalciferol is an effective treatment for vitamin D deficiency, the current K/DOQI guidelines do not provide sufficient evidence to support increasing the dose of vitamin D or using higher dosages. Further research is required to determine the optimal treatment strategy and its impact on clinical outcomes in CKD patients with vitamin D deficiency.
